Plain curl GETs (BandOnTheMap-SourceInvestigation/0.1 UA) of https://www.wow.pt (301 redirect to /en/), https://www.wow.pt/pt/ (site's own PT homepage), and the given candidate events_url https://www.wow.pt/pt/agenda-cultural all returned an empty React client-rendered shell: a bare `
`, an inline script literally computing `INLINED_PAGE_TYPE = JSON.parse(''.replace(...))` (an empty string — nothing inlined), three webpack chunk `

Fetched the same public page's own referenced webpack runtime and client JS bundles (per Level 2 guidance: public JS/bootstrap data and publicly-referenced endpoints). The client bundle fingerprints Magento Open Source + PWA Studio (Apollo Client GraphQL query documents against storeConfig/customer/ProductInterface/CategoryInterface/CmsPage, and a client-side router with RootCmp_CMS_PAGE/RootCmp_CATEGORY/RootCmp_PRODUCT route types) and constructs its GraphQL client as `new URL("/graphql", origin)`. A plain, read-only, unauthenticated `availableStores` query against https://www.wow.pt/graphql confirmed four store views (en/pt/es/fr). Using a `Store: pt` request header (the storefront's own documented multi-store mechanism, not a bypass of anything), a read-only `urlResolver` query for the GIVEN candidate lead path ("agenda-cultural") returned `null` — this path does not resolve to any page in the PT store at all, confirming the candidate lead is a dead/stale URL, independently of the fact that it happens to return HTTP 200 (every route on this SPA returns the same generic shell regardless of validity; only urlResolver reveals whether client-side routing would actually render a page or a 404). A second `urlResolver` query for "experiencias/agenda" (found in the retained client bundle's own old-URL-to-new-URL redirect map, which repeatedly points several legacy paths at "/experience/agenda?ticket_type[filter]=...") resolved to `{type: CATEGORY, id: 163}` — a real, live page. Read-only `category`/`products`/`aggregations` queries against category 163 (named 'Agenda', url_path 'o-que-fazer-no-wow/agenda', 19 products) retrieved the full bounded product list and its own facet/attribute aggregations. The facets are: price, category_uid (Museus/Restaurantes/Pink Palace/Gastronomia e Eventos/Workshops/etc.), time_of_day, visitor_type (Criança/Adulto/Família), and ticket_type (Destaques/Museus/Workshops/Gatronomia & Eventos/Bilhetes Conjuntos) — none of which is a live-music/concert-specific filter. Drilling into the two candidate sub-buckets most likely to carry music content (category 438, the 'Agenda' sub-category proper, 8 products — all museum tickets/workshops/membership card, zero music; and category 453 'Gastronomia e Eventos', 6 products: a Fado dinner-show, a comedy-club night, a film-club series, Oktoberfest, a dinner-theatre show, and a recurring 'sunset' session) confirmed the catalog mixes hospitality/exhibition/workshop programming with only incidental, dinner-bundled music content, never as its own filterable category. One sampled product's own categories field (Fado Show & Dinner) lists only Restaurantes/Visita o WOW/Agenda/Gastronomia e Eventos — no music-specific tag. This already fully answers identity, platform classification, data-path discovery, and field/content assessment (including the decisive content-scope finding) without needing any JS execution or browser session, so escalation to Level 3 (BROWSER_OBSERVATION) was not attempted.

venue_reference: WOW — World of Wine — a large cultural quarter (museums, restaurants, bars, and event spaces) on the Vila Nova de Gaia riverfront, Cais de Gaia, Vila Nova de Gaia, Portugal (Porto metropolitan catchment). Referenced loose lead: sources/porto.json's 'wow-world-of-wine-gaia' entry (not edited by this investigation).

identity.notes: https://www.wow.pt was given as the loose lead's official website and this investigation independently re-confirmed it from its own retained evidence, not merely assumed. The retained PT homepage's own `og:title`/`og:description` meta tags self-identify as 'WOW Porto - The Cultural District' / 'WOW Porto - O Distrito Cultural' — 'Cluster of museums, restaurants & bars in cellars, telling the story of Porto's port wine industry' / 'Conjunto de museus, restaurantes e bares nas caves, contando a história da indústria do vinho do Porto' — matching the candidate's own self-description as a large Vila Nova de Gaia riverfront cultural quarter. The retained GraphQL storeConfig response self-reports `base_url`/`secure_base_url` as `https://www.wow.pt/`, a same-domain, self-referential confirmation. No street address or postal code was found in the retained static evidence (the address itself is rendered client-side, not present in the retained HTML/JSON, since the whole storefront is a client-rendered SPA) — recorded honestly as a minor gap rather than guessed.

site_classification.platform: Magento Open Source storefront running PWA Studio (a React single-page app served as static webpack chunks — runtime/vendors/client — with Apollo Client GraphQL queries against a standard Magento GraphQL schema: storeConfig, customer, ProductInterface, CategoryInterface, CmsPage, urlResolver). Front end is fully client-rendered (empty `<div id="root">` shell, confirmed at Level 1). Backend is a separate, publicly reachable GraphQL API at https://www.wow.pt/graphql, unauthenticated, supporting ordinary read-only queries (availableStores, urlResolver, category, products, aggregations) when a `Store` request header selects the desired storefront locale (en/pt/es/fr). This is a genuine e-commerce/ticketing catalog API (Magento's product/category model), not an events-specific schema — there is no dedicated Event/Concert GraphQL type; 'events' in this source's own vocabulary means a purchasable admission ticket (a Magento Product) filed under ordinary catalog categories.

GRAPHQL_CATEGORY_PRODUCT_LISTING (checked — a real, reachable, well-structured public API, but its content is a generic multi-attraction ticketed-admissions catalog, not a filterable live-music/concert event listing)

title.notes: The value shown is the one sampled product's own GraphQL `name` field, used representatively (per this record's v1.2 requirement that a PROVEN entry carry an actual non-null value, unlike v1.1's aggregate-finding convention seen in fama-dalfama-lisbon-01). Every one of the 19 retained products in category 163 ('Agenda') carries a non-empty `name` field directly (e.g. this one, 'COMEDY CLUB NO ANGEL'S SHARE - 17 SETEMBRO', 'OKTOBERFEST - 2 A 5 OUTUBRO'), mechanically confirmed 19/19 non-empty in evidence/offline-proof-output.txt. This field being technically extractable does not by itself make the source a genuine music-event candidate — see decision below.

start_date.notes: Several product names embed a day-of-month + month-name fragment directly in free text (e.g. '25 SETEMBRO', '17 SETEMBRO', '2 A 5 OUTUBRO') — but no year is stated anywhere in connection with any of these dates. None of the 19 product names contains a 4-digit year at all (mechanically confirmed, 0/19). The one sampled product's free-text description (Fado Show & Dinner) does contain two 4-digit numbers, but they are wine-vintage years in the dinner-pairing menu text ('Sílica Branco 2023', 'São Lourenço Tinto 2019') — unrelated to the event's own date — mechanically confirmed by evidence/offline-proof.mjs, which checks specifically that no year appears near the description's actual time statement ('a partir das 20h') and that the only years present anywhere are exactly those two wine vintages. This is exactly the negative example this project's own policy names explicitly (docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's v1.2 worked-examples table: a bare day+month with no page/section year context must stay AMBIGUOUS/UNKNOWN, never promoted to a claimed year via AI plausibility). Unlike fama-dalfama-lisbon-01 (an explicit 'AGOSTO 2026' heading) or the example-deterministic-context-ready-01 fixture (an explicit 'September 2026' heading), no retained WOW evidence states a governing year anywhere, so DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT is genuinely unavailable here, not merely unused.

time.notes: One sampled product's free-text description (Fado Show & Dinner) states 'Uma experiência a não perder, a partir das 20h' (from 20h) — a genuine, explicit local time statement, but embedded in unstructured marketing/menu prose, not a structured field, and only checked for this single sampled product (1 of 19) — not verified as systematically present across the catalog. No UTC offset or IANA timezone is stated anywhere.

end.notes: No end time or duration was found anywhere in any retained evidence file (product names, descriptions, or category data).

venue_location.notes: The overall complex identity and city (WOW, Vila Nova de Gaia riverfront) is established via `identity` above, but no structural, per-product location field was found in the retained GraphQL schema fields queried (categories only name generic catalog groupings like 'Restaurantes', not a specific room/space). The one sampled Fado product's free-text description names a specific dining room ('o restaurante 1828 na sala privada Dona Maria') — but this is unstructured prose, observed for only 1 of 19 sampled products, not a systematic per-record field.

source_record_id.notes: Every product's own GraphQL `id` (a Magento internal product id, e.g. 22663 for the Fado product) is present directly and was empirically cross-checked via two independent query paths for one sampled product: the category-163 `products()` list query and a separate `urlResolver(url: "fado-show-and-dinner")` lookup both returned id 22663 (1/1 cross-checked, matching this project's stable-identifier rule's empirical-proof clause — a smaller sample than coliseu-ageas-porto-01's 2/2, honestly noted). The product's own `url_key` is additionally the source's own canonical routing key (confirmed live via urlResolver to resolve to `{type: PRODUCT, id: 22663}`), satisfying the rule's third clause (a permalink-style slug the source itself uses as its canonical path).

event_url.notes: A canonical detail-page URL is directly constructible as https://www.wow.pt/pt/{url_key} (e.g. https://www.wow.pt/pt/fado-show-and-dinner) — confirmed live: `urlResolver(url: "fado-show-and-dinner")` (with `Store: pt`) resolves to `{type: PRODUCT, id: 22663, redirectCode: 0}`, matching the same product id found via the category listing, and a direct curl GET of the constructed URL returned 200 OK (the same client-rendered shell as every other route, honestly noted — the page itself still requires client-side rendering to display content; only the URL's validity/routing is proven server-side).

price.notes: The one sampled product's `price_range.minimum_price.regular_price` returned `{value: 0, currency: "EUR"}` — but this is almost certainly an artefact of the product being a configurable/bundle product whose real price depends on unselected options (date/party-size), not a genuine EUR 0 / free admission. This investigation did not resolve the real per-occurrence ticket price, and explicitly did NOT promote the literal '0' to a claimed FREE/PROVEN value, since doing so would misrepresent what the source actually guarantees.

blockers.description: This candidate's genuine, reachable 'Agenda' data path (Magento category 163) is a generic ticketed-admissions catalog for the entire multi-attraction complex — day passes, museum tickets, kids' workshops, an annual membership card — not a music-event listing. Its own facet/attribute taxonomy (ticket_type: Destaques/Museus/Workshops/Gatronomia & Eventos/Bilhetes Conjuntos; category_uid: Museus/Restaurantes/Pink Palace/etc.) contains no dedicated, filterable live-music/concert category anywhere. The closest bucket, 'Gastronomia e Eventos' (6 products), mixes a Fado dinner-show with a comedy-club night, a film-club series, Oktoberfest, and a dinner-theatre show — genuinely incidental music content bundled into dinner/hospitality packages, not a standalone concert programme. Per this project's own scope rule (do not treat restaurants/bars as candidates merely because they occasionally host music), and per this task's explicit instruction to only recommend activation when a genuinely identifiable, filterable music-event category or listing exists, this candidate fails that bar. This is a content-scope/suitability finding, not a technical acquisition failure — the GraphQL API itself is real, reachable, and well-structured (see site_classification, data_paths, and several PROVEN field_assessment entries above).

Even for the small number of genuinely music-adjacent products (Fado Show & Dinner, Comedy Club, Oktoberfest), no retained evidence anywhere states a year for the stated day/month — start_date can only honestly reach AMBIGUOUS, not PROVEN, for any of them under this project's date/time rule.

The given loose lead's events_url (https://www.wow.pt/pt/agenda-cultural) does not resolve to any page in this store at all (urlResolver returns null) — it is a dead/stale URL and must not be reused as-is if this candidate is ever reconsidered; the real, resolvable path is the 'experiencias/agenda' -> category 163 route discovered by this investigation.

reasons: identity.status is PROVEN (this really is WOW's own official site, independently re-confirmed from retained evidence) and site_classification.acquisition_class is PUBLIC_JSON_API (a real, reachable, well-structured public GraphQL API was genuinely discovered and queried) — so this REJECT is NOT an identity or technical-acquisition failure, unlike this repository's other REJECTed candidates (le-divan-du-monde-paris-01, le-reservoir-paris-01, musik-frieden-berlin-01), which all failed because no live first-party site/content existed at all.

The given candidate lead URL (https://www.wow.pt/pt/agenda-cultural) is itself a dead lead: mechanically proven via a live, read-only GraphQL urlResolver query returning null for that exact path — it does not resolve to any page in the store, despite returning HTTP 200 (every SPA route does, regardless of validity).

This investigation independently discovered the real, resolvable events/ticketing listing (Magento category 163, 'Agenda', 19 products) and inspected it in full, including its own facet/attribute taxonomy (ticket_type, category_uid, time_of_day, visitor_type) — and found NO dedicated, filterable live-music/concert category anywhere in the source's own structure. The listing is a generic ticketed-admissions catalog spanning museum entry, kids' workshops, day passes, and an annual membership card, with genuinely music-adjacent content (a Fado dinner-show, a comedy-club night) appearing only incidentally, bundled inside a mixed 'Gastronomia e Eventos' (Gastronomy & Events) dinner/hospitality bucket alongside a film-club series and Oktoberfest — never as its own filterable category.

Per this task's explicit instruction and this project's existing scope rule (do not treat restaurants/bars as candidates merely because they occasionally host music, generalised here to a whole cultural-quarter ticketing catalog that occasionally bundles a dinner-show), only a genuinely identifiable, filterable music-event category or listing would justify activation — this candidate does not have one, so activation is not recommended.

collector_assessment.blockers contains a CRITICAL entry describing this content-scope failure precisely, plus a MAJOR entry noting that even the few music-adjacent products lack a stated year anywhere in retained evidence (start_date can only honestly reach AMBIGUOUS).

This decision does not claim the technical work was wasted: several field_assessment entries (title, source_record_id, event_url) are honestly PROVEN, demonstrating the API itself is genuinely usable — the rejection is specifically about content scope/suitability for this project's music-event-source purpose, not acquisition feasibility.

evidence/offline-proof.mjs + evidence/offline-proof-output.txt provide a DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION evidence item: a dependency-free, no-network re-parse of every retained fixture that mechanically reproduces the empty-shell finding, the dead-lead-vs-real-category urlResolver contrast, the full facet-label scan (confirming no music/concert-specific filter exists), the year-absence scan across all product names/descriptions, and the id-stability cross-check for the one sampled product.

This decision is a research conclusion only — it does not edit sources/*.json or any registry. If WOW ever adds a genuinely dedicated, filterable concert/live-music listing, a NEW investigation (citing supersedes: "wow-world-of-wine-gaia-01") would be required, never a rewrite of this record.

evidence.description: Raw retained response to a read-only GraphQL `products(filter: {category_id: {eq: "163"}, ticket_type: {eq: "238"}})` query — the 'Destaques' (Highlights) facet, the closest thing to a 'featured events' filter this source has: 10 products spanning day passes, a museum exhibition, sunset DJ sessions, comedy club, Fado dinner, Oktoberfest, dinner theatre, wine-cellar passes, and the annual membership card — confirming even the 'Highlights' filter is generic, not music-specific.
evidence.method: curl -sS -D headers-graphql-highlights.txt -o body-graphql-highlights.json --max-time 20 -A "BandOnTheMap-SourceInvestigation/0.1 (+https://github.com/chriswatson6675/band_on_the_map)" -H "Store: pt" -G --data-urlencode "query=query{products(filter:{category_id:{eq:\"163\"},ticket_type:{eq:\"238\"}},pageSize:25){total_count items{id name url_key}}}"
